title: Noach: whole-hearted (Genesis 6:9)
hookLine: the portion opens by calling Noah tamim, whole

lines: A MOMENT WITH ALL OF YOU.
ONE WORD FOR A WHOLE PERSON.
cards: Lunch eaten while answering email. A friend heard while half-reading a text. A show watched while scrolling another screen.

A lot of life gets done with part of you, and the rest somewhere else. And then there are moments done with all of a person: holding a newborn, playing music, a conversation so good the time disappears.
The second portion of the Torah describes its hero with a Hebrew word for exactly that.

teach.b: The portion is called Noach, Noah, and it begins: "These are the generations of Noah. Noah was in his generations a man righteous and whole-hearted; Noah walked with God."
There's yesterday's phrase again: walked with God. And there's today's word.

Whole-hearted, in Hebrew, is tamim: whole, complete, without a crack. The same word describes an animal fit for an offering: unblemished, nothing missing. Later, God tells Abraham, walk before me and be tamim.
And Moses tells the people, "Thou shalt be whole-hearted with the LORD thy God."
It's not a word for perfect, as in never making mistakes. It's a word for undivided: all of you, in one place.

teach.h: IN HIS GENERATIONS: PRAISE OR LIMIT?
teach.b: Then the rabbis notice two small words: in his generations. Why add that? The Talmud records a disagreement.

One teacher says it's praise: if Noah was righteous even in a violent generation, imagine him in a good one. Another says it's a limit: righteous for his generation; in Abraham's time, he wouldn't have stood out.
Rashi quotes both, and doesn't choose. Either way, the text sets Noah's wholeness in a world coming apart. The verses right after say the earth was filled with violence.
In the middle of that, one person was undivided. That's what tamim asks. Not perfection.
Wholeness, in whatever generation you're in.

how: Parashat Noach, Genesis 6:9–11:32, is read on the second Shabbat after Simchat Torah; teachers often begin with the debate over 'in his generations' in Rashi and the Talmud.

o: perfect, never making a single mistake
whole and undivided, all of you in one place
humble and quiet, never seeking praise

games.q: inside the word — tap the pairs.

s: tamim means never making a mistake
it means whole, undivided: all of you in one place.
the rabbis disagree whether 'in his generations' is praise
one says praise, one says a limit; Rashi quotes both.
the same verse says Noah walked with God
the phrase used for Enoch comes back for Noah.

games.q: the Torah says Noah was righteous 'in his generations'. you're a rabbi in the study hall. how do you read it?
o: as praise: righteous even in a violent time.
as a limit: only righteous compared to his time.
games.why: the Talmud records both readings, and Rashi quotes both without choosing.

practice: Notice where the parts of you are: some in this room, some in a worry about tomorrow, some in a conversation from yesterday.
Call each part back, one at a time, like calling people to the table, and be here, all of you, for one breath, then another. If a part wanders off, call it back without scolding.

wordCard.voice: Tamim. Whole, complete, undivided: the word the Torah uses for Noah, and for being whole-hearted with God.

carryVoice: Your line: whole-hearted. All of you, gathered in one place. See you on the ark, tomorrow.
